---
title: "Firm-pair probabilities and report-card blocks"
subtitle: "5.4 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Figure 5A"
description: "Comparison of isolated-pair thresholds with the relations in KRW's coherent cards."
---

Each cell gives the posterior probability that the row firm's contact gap is larger than the column firm's gap.
Darker blue indicates stronger support for that direction. The threshold shows which directions would minimize
loss if each pair were decided on its own. The grade blocks show what the archived report actually states.
Some high-probability directions lie within a grade and are withheld. Some directions between grades fall short
of the pairwise threshold. Select a cell or choose two firms to read their comparison above the matrix.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **All direction probabilities.** The Blues legend reads “Pr(row truly higher)”. Arrow keys move through every
  cell, including the diagonal. Each cell names both firms and gives their relation in the card.
- **Above the threshold.** At λ .25, the corresponding withholding cost is τ .20. The strict pairwise rule
  would state 1,575 pairs whose favored direction has probability above .80. Other cells fade, while the gray
  diagonal continues to mark self-comparisons.
- **Add the card blocks.** Orange hatching marks 575 confident pairs withheld within a grade. Purple outlines
  mark 324 stated pairs whose error exceeds τ. The discrepancies can arise from requiring one coherent report,
  even with no grade cap.
- **λ .50 blocks.** The threshold admits 2,994 pairs. Of these, 49 are withheld by the card; 545 stated pairs have
  error above the current τ. Varying the reward changes both the threshold and the selected archived card.
- **Gender blocks.** The target is the signed male-name contact advantage. Negative gaps favor
  female-named applicants. Both row-above-column directions retain this signed orientation.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
KRW's code selected the grid cards using their archived probabilities and solver tolerances. The app holds those
grades fixed and evaluates them with the released postrank probabilities. The baseline race card is in Figure 7,
and the gender card is in Figure 14 (§VIII). Figures 5A and 6 are in §V.E, and Figure 10A is in §VI.B.
